newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht sales ease after central bank denial.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht sales ease after central bank denial.

text.p: Selling pressure on the Thai baht eased on Thursday after the Bank of Thailand denied market rumours that its governor Rerngchai Marakanond might resign, dealers said.
The baht firmed to 25.948/25.953 against the dollar at midday from 25.960/25.970 in early morning trade, they told Reuters.
"Dollar buying against the baht eased relatively after the central bank's denial," said a dealer at a European bank.
The baht came under renewed selling pressure in early trade on Thursday after some Thai business newspapers speculated that the central bank governor might resign, dealers said.
A senior central bank official categorically denied the reports.

Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan also said that he saw no reason for Marakanond to resign over a government decision to suspend his deputy who handled a bungled court case against executives of Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc.
Amnuay told reporters: "I would like to make it clear that this is unfounded and there is no reason for the governor to resign."
